scope: Read-only review of final independent native-3D design captures; no source, bundle or data modifications
observedPasses: All five capture files declare native3D=true and no model-loader warnings. Source metadata identifies current production raphael-polish.glb, locomotion-v9 and hairstyles-v3-refined, not legacy sprite characters.
All groups include the actual first/second/third sword-cut clips; W07 metadata includes36 sampled Draw weights and four real Draw morph meshes.
Bow volley frame00347 shows distinct physical arrow paths toward separate targets.
Thunder frames00134 and00333 show a visibly continuous strong primary trunk with subordinate branches and recognizable contact nodes; no disconnected thin-spark confetti.
The fire meteor is a continuous flame-covered body with no exposed rock or black smoke; casting circle and ultimate role are present.
Ground, hero, enemies and retreat space remain visible in the inspected representative frames.
WAR and FIR required visual fixes were independently rechecked in recaptured representative frames and are resolved there.
Both replacement reel captures are complete: WAR514 frames and FIR541 frames, with capture metadata finalized after the last frame.

requiredFixes.finding: At the inspected extended-sweep phases, the bright blade surface rises into or above the top title band and is visibly separated in screen space from the current hand-held sword. Its narrow pale sheet does not consistently convey a broad heavy close-range strike.
requiredFixes.requestedCorrection: Constrain extension from the native weapon trajectory, reduce upward projection and establish a connected forward lateral pressure arc; then re-capture WAR.
requiredFixes.resolutionObserved: The close weapon ribbon now remains near the actual sword path. Forward lateral pressure arcs separately express the enlarged visual reach. The previously tall detached blade sheet no longer clips into the top label band in inspected recaptures.

requiredFixes.finding: The incoming meteor head is visible but much of its body/tail is clipped behind the top label area. The main impact at frame00361 is compact relative to the large aiming circle, and the low wave at00364 is pale/pink and softer than the requested substantial orange-red terminal burst.
requiredFixes.requestedCorrection: Lower the visible descent path or shorten its early tail and strengthen the concentrated orange-red main burst while preserving ground/targets; then re-capture FIR.
requiredFixes.resolutionObserved: The shortened-to-lengthening incoming comet is visible within the scene and descends to the target. The recaptured main burst has substantially greater orange-red volume and a concentrated hot core; later low rolls remain translucent enough to distinguish targets. Inspected main body and crest no longer cut into the top title band.

limits: Only representative stills, two six-sample transition boards and capture metadata were inspected, not all 2436 frames or complete reel playback. Smooth full-motion continuity and every individual contact moment are not certified by this review.
The preview uses genuine current3D assets in a standalone Three.js design renderer, not the Cocos/TapTap runtime; lights and staging differ.
Enemies are the current raider3D model with its existing dark outfit, not the armored enemies in earlier concept boards.
Capture JSON does not contain a separate browser-pageerror list, so the recorded empty warnings establish model-loader warning status only.
User art acceptance, production integration, damage/range balance, performance and true-device acceptance remain unverified.

internalStaticArtReview: No remaining blocking visual defect found in the inspected representative recaptures; not a blanket acceptance of every frame or full-motion smoothness.

reviewedFrozenBundle.note: Bundle observed at revision-review time; capture files do not independently embed a bundle hash.

remainingArtReviewNotes: The enlarged fire peak temporarily obscures portions of back-row enemy bodies; silhouettes/heads and foreground targets remain readable in inspected stills. User should judge its density in motion.
The forward pressure arc is an explicit added skill-design effect distinct from the near-sword trail; it must not be described as an exact existing damage boundary.
Full37-skill motion playback, every frame-to-frame transition and every weapon/contact moment were not exhaustively reviewed.

representativeTransitionReview.scope: Two short sampled transition segments only; six unmodified captured-frame crops each, laid out with Pillow. No source, renderer, bundle or skill data changed.

items.scope: Six fixed-camera crops from actual captured3D frames; no redraw or interpolation

review.result: No obvious standing-pose reset, hero position snap, or detached tall blade-sheet reappearance in these six samples.
observations: The hero remains planted and follows through from a low extended cut into the raised second-cut preparation and a lower finishing sweep.
The compact weapon-adjacent ribbon follows the changing sword posture. Forward pressure arcs travel and fade separately at a low scene height, with readable target-contact sparks.
The samples are spaced three capture frames apart and cannot establish whether an unsampled single-frame discontinuity exists.

items.scope: Six fixed-camera crops from actual captured3D frames; no redraw or interpolation

review.result: No obvious caster-pose reset, relocated impact origin, or missing intermediate stage in these six samples.
observations: The small incoming flame body grows and reaches the aiming region; the next samples show the main orange-red crown followed by outward low rolling fire and a fading core.
The effect remains anchored to the same ground area and the caster keeps a stable foot position. The aiming ornament fades as the impact and expanding boundary take over.

The crest briefly obscures parts of the back row; foreground targets remain distinguishable. The broad low flame shape persists over the last two samples, so its hold and decay timing still require playback and user art review.
The samples are spaced about five to six capture frames apart and do not certify smoothness of each atlas crossfade.

representativeTransitionReview.conclusion: No additional blocking jump was apparent in these representative sampled transitions. This is not full-reel or every-frame visual acceptance.
